caseStudies.title: Confidential vECUs with Arm CCA
caseStudies.subtitle: Automotive virtual ECU research using Zephyr OS and Arm CCA.
caseStudies.problem: Automotive virtual ECU research requires integrating operating systems and isolation mechanisms that were not designed as a single stack. Zephyr OS and Arm CCA presented compatibility gaps.
caseStudies.approach: Use a custom shim layer to bridge integration incompatibilities in an automotive vECU research platform for mixed-criticality workloads.
caseStudies.contribution: Developed the vECU research platform and addressed Zephyr OS–Arm CCA integration through a custom shim layer.
caseStudies.outcome: An automotive vECU research platform supporting the ongoing systems-security investigation.
caseStudies.limits: Ongoing research; detailed security and performance evaluation is outside this public overview.

caseStudies.title: Split ML-KEM in TrustZone
caseStudies.subtitle: Secret-dependent ML-KEM partitioning on Arm TrustZone-A.
caseStudies.problem: Placing a full post-quantum cryptographic implementation inside an embedded TEE can enlarge the trusted code base and increase execution cost.
caseStudies.approach: Partition ML-KEM by secret dependency: isolate secret-dependent operations in OP-TEE’s Secure World and offload public computation to the Normal World.
caseStudies.contribution: Implemented split ML-KEM in OP-TEE on Arm TrustZone-A and evaluated the partitioned architecture. Co-first author of the KCC 2026 paper.
caseStudies.outcome: The reported evaluation reduced trusted code size by 90.8% and mean latency by 25.5% relative to the study’s baseline architecture. The research received the KCC 2026 Outstanding Paper Award.
caseStudies.limits: These are baseline-relative results from the study’s evaluated platform and configuration, not general guarantees for every device or implementation. Public repositories include related research prototypes and scaffolding.

caseStudies.title: SCAN
caseStudies.subtitle: Structural clustering and adaptive thresholds for Android malware under concept drift.
caseStudies.problem: Android malware classifiers must contend with evolving feature distributions and class imbalance over time. A decision rule fitted to one period may become less reliable in later data.
caseStudies.approach: Use Gaussian mixture clustering to model structure and adaptive thresholds to support malware classification under concept drift and class imbalance.
caseStudies.contribution: Designed SCAN and published the framework as first author in Computer Modeling in Engineering & Sciences.
caseStudies.outcome: The reported evaluation achieved average accuracy and F1 scores above 91% across six years.
caseStudies.limits: The reported averages describe the study’s datasets and evaluation protocol; they do not guarantee performance on every future malware distribution.

caseStudies.title: ALARM
caseStudies.subtitle: Android malware detection with Leiden clustering and mixture-of-experts classification.
caseStudies.problem: Changing Android malware distributions can weaken the assumptions of a single classifier. The research investigates whether API relationships and community structure can support more adaptive detection.
caseStudies.approach: Combine Leiden-based community clustering with mixture-of-experts classification in an Android malware detection framework. This differs from SCAN’s Gaussian mixture clustering and adaptive-threshold approach.
caseStudies.contribution: Extended API co-occurrence graph and community-based detection with a mixture-of-experts model, and published ALARM as first author at ACM SAC 2026.
caseStudies.outcome: Published in the Proceedings of the 41st ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing, Thessaloniki, Greece.
caseStudies.limits: Robustness depends on the datasets, drift conditions, and evaluation protocol. The paper provides the full experimental setup.
